vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 59070 / ARVO arvo:59070 / openexr Classifier_read stack-buffer-overflow

project.name: OpenEXR
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout inside the running container is on commit `7c40603eb2812148c6a99fbb6ee07533395fdadb`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the pre-fix `len += 1; if (len == 128 + 1)` ordering in `Classifier_read`; the fix hunk in `patch.diff` applies the same logic with a slightly different function signature.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 59070 (openexr): AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 130 in `Classifier_read`, reached from `DwaCompressor_readChannelRules -> DwaCompressor_uncompress -> internal_exr_undo_dwaa`.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / `file gt_results/arvo_59070/poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the staged 450-byte OpenEXR version-2 scanline DWAA witness with SHA-256 `36c173f3cb2478c196ea41feb242a1156fae56fb0dd06892d52defc53d84d6c0`. On the crashing path, `DwaCompressor_readChannelRules()` reads the attacker-controlled rule-section size, seeds `tmpPtr`/`dataSize` for the rule block, and then iterates `while (rv == EXR_ERR_SUCCESS && dataSize > 0)` calling `Classifier_read(&tmpc, &tmpPtr, &dataSize)` over successive classifier records. The saved ASan stack fixes the crash to that loop call site at `internal_dwa_compressor.h:1526`, but not to a specific loop ordinal, so earlier successful iterations may already have advanced `tmpPtr` and reduced `dataSize` before the crashing call. On the crashing iteration, the current classifier record presented to `Classifier_read()` supplies 129 consecutive non-NUL suffix bytes, so the local `suffix[129]` stack array fills completely and the loop leaves `len == 129`. The vulnerable code then executes `len += 1` before checking `if (len == 128 + 1) return EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK;`, so the exactly-full unterminated suffix is not rejected and the copy length becomes 130. `internal_exr_alloc(len)` allocates 130 bytes and `memcpy(mem, suffix, len)` reads 130 bytes from the 129-byte stack buffer, producing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ. The fix moves the full-buffer rejection ahead of the increment so a full 129-byte unterminated suffix is rejected as corrupt chunk data.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the crashing path that reads the attacker-controlled DWAA channel-rule byte count from the compressed chunk and materializes parser state for the classifier records.
source.value_from: The staged witness is exactly `gt_results/arvo_59070/poc`, a 450-byte file with SHA-256 `36c173f3cb2478c196ea41feb242a1156fae56fb0dd06892d52defc53d84d6c0`. Local `file(1)` identifies it as `OpenEXR image data, version 2, storage: scanline, compression: dwaa`. After header parsing, `decompress_data()` dispatches the packed chunk to `internal_exr_undo_dwaa()`, and this statement reads the leading 16-bit rule-section length from that attacker-controlled DWAA rule block.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This loop consumes attacker-controlled bytes from the classifier record passed to the crashing `Classifier_read()` call and materializes them into the local `suffix[129]` buffer while advancing `len`. On the witnessed crash path, that record has no NUL within its first 129 suffix bytes, so the stack buffer fills completely and `len` reaches 129.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the off-by-one length update, `memcpy` reads 130 bytes from the 129-byte stack buffer `suffix`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace says `READ of size 130` at this line and identifies `suffix` in the `DwaCompressor_readChannelRules` frame as the overflown stack object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `Classifier_read()` adds space for a terminator before checking whether the 129-byte temporary suffix buffer was completely filled. When the crashing classifier record occupies all 129 bytes, `len` becomes 130 and the subsequent `len == 128 + 1` guard misses the full-buffer case instead of rejecting it.
root_cause.note: The fix moves the `len == 128 + 1` rejection ahead of `len += 1`, which preserves the intended corrupt-chunk check for a full, unterminated suffix.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is an OpenEXR scanline image with DWAA compression, so after header parsing and chunk loading `decompress_data()` takes the `EXR_COMPRESSION_DWAA` case and admits the packed chunk into the DWA decompressor that later reaches `DwaCompressor_readChannelRules()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The DWA rule parser reads the attacker-controlled 16-bit byte count for the channel-rule section from the compressed chunk. This is the first project-side materialization of the rule data later consumed by `Classifier_read()`.

For the witnessed crash the availability check succeeds, so the parser strips the 2-byte size field and seeds the scan with `tmpPtr` at the first classifier record and `dataSize` equal to the remaining rule-block byte count. This is only the loop's initial state: if earlier iterations succeed, later calls will inherit updated `tmpPtr`/`dataSize` values.

The scan loop repeatedly calls `Classifier_read()` on the current `tmpPtr`/`dataSize`. On each successful earlier iteration, `Classifier_read()` returns through `*ptr = curin; *size -= len + 2 * sizeof (uint8_t);` at lines 117-118, advancing those caller variables to the next record. The saved stack pins the crash to line 1526 inside this loop, so the crashing call consumes the loop-carried current `tmpPtr`/`dataSize` state, which may already reflect zero or more successful prior records.

Using the current `*ptr`/`*size` passed by the crashing loop iteration, `Classifier_read()` materializes that classifier record's suffix into the fixed 129-byte stack array `suffix`. On the witnessed crash path, the current record has no NUL within its first 129 bytes, and the present size guard `len > (*size - 3)` never fires, so the loop exits only because `len` reaches 129 after filling `suffix[0..128]`.

Root cause. After step 4 leaves `len == 129`, this code adds one before checking the full-buffer case, so `len` becomes 130 and the `len == 129` rejection is false. The exactly-full, unterminated suffix therefore survives as if it had room for a terminator.

Sink. With `len` now 130, the destination allocation is 130 bytes and `memcpy` attempts to read 130 bytes from the 129-byte stack buffer `suffix`. ASan reports `READ of size 130` here and points at `suffix` in the `DwaCompressor_readChannelRules` frame as the overflown object.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_59070 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/openexr_exrcorecheck_fuzzer` and produced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 130` with stack `Classifier_read -> DwaCompressor_readChannelRules -> DwaCompressor_uncompress`.

format.name: OpenEXR DWAA scanline witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 450-byte file with SHA-256 `36c173f3cb2478c196ea41feb242a1156fae56fb0dd06892d52defc53d84d6c0`. Local `file(1)` identifies it as `OpenEXR image data, version 2, storage: scanline, compression: dwaa`. To reach the witnessed sink, this exact file's DWAA channel-rule block must eventually make one crashing `Classifier_read()` iteration consume 129 consecutive non-NUL suffix bytes before the two trailing classifier bytes, so the local `suffix[129]` buffer fills completely and the vulnerable `len += 1` path copies 130 bytes from it. This contract is limited to this staged witness and does not generalize to other OpenEXR files or other DWAA rule blocks.
